question: If a constant force of 10 N moves an object 5 m in the direction of the force, find the work done.
solution:
The correct answer is __**50 J**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Work** is defined as the transfer of energy that occurs when a force is applied to an object causing displacement in the direction of the force.
 
• The formula to calculate work is:

 **Work = Force × Displacement × cos(θ)**, where:
 
 
• **Force (F):** The magnitude of the applied force, measured in **Newtons (N)**.
 
• **Displacement (d):** The distance moved by the object in the direction of the force, measured in **meters (m)**.
 
• **θ (Theta):** The angle between the force and displacement. Here, the force is applied in the same direction as the displacement, so θ = 0°.
 
 
 
• In this question:
 
 
• **Force (F):** 10 N
 
• **Displacement (d):** 5 m
 
• **cos(θ):** cos(0°) = 1
 
 
 
• Substituting into the formula:

 Work = 10 × 5 × 1 = 50 J
 
• **Hence, the total work done is 50 Joules.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Work:**

 
 
• Work is a scalar quantity and its unit in the International System of Units (SI) is the **Joule (J)**.
 
• 1 Joule is defined as the work done when a force of 1 Newton displaces an object by 1 meter in the direction of the force.
 
• Work can be positive, negative, or zero depending on the direction of the force and displacement:
 
 
• **Positive Work:** When force and displacement are in the same direction (θ = 0°).
 
• **Negative Work:** When force and displacement are in opposite directions (θ = 180°).
 
• **Zero Work:** When the force is perpendicular to the displacement (θ = 90°).
 
 
 
 
 
• **Applications of Work:**
 
 
• Work is used in calculating energy transfer in mechanical systems like lifting objects, moving vehicles, etc.
 
• It helps in determining the energy consumption in machines and engines.
 
 
 
• **Related Concepts:**
 
 
• **Power:** The rate at which work is done, measured in Watts (W).
 
• **Energy:** The capacity to do work, which includes potential energy, kinetic energy, and thermal energy.
 
• **Force:** A push or pull exerted on an object, measured in Newtons (N).
 
 
 
• **Examples of Work:**
 
 
• Pushing a box across a floor.
 
• Lifting a weight against gravity.
 
• Pulling a cart in a straight direction.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• When no displacement occurs, no work is done even if a force is applied (e.g., pushing a wall).
 
• Work is maximum when the force is applied in the exact direction of displacement (θ = 0°).
 
• Work depends only on the component of force in the direction of displacement.
 
• The concept of work is fundamental in understanding energy transfer in mechanical systems and thermodynamics.
